justification_text:
My point estimates reflect a broadly stable near-term outlook with only modest drift upward over time. At the one-day horizon, the estimate of 578 was anchored heavily on recent observed values and short-term momentum, essentially assuming that whatever level was recently realized would persist with only minor mean-reverting or trending adjustment. At the one-week horizon, the slight uptick to 580 reflects a small positive drift assumption, perhaps based on a gentle underlying trend or seasonal tendency. By one month, the estimate rises marginally further to 585, incorporating the idea that whatever gradual directional pressure exists has more time to accumulate, though the magnitude of expected change remains quite modest relative to the uncertainty involved.

The confidence interval widths reflect the natural scaling of uncertainty with time horizon. At one day, the 90% interval of 560–596 is relatively tight because there is limited time for new information or shocks to materialize. By one week, the interval widens to 548–612, incorporating the possibility of a meaningful data release, policy signal, or market repricing event occurring within that window. At one month, the interval expands substantially to 520–650, acknowledging that over four weeks a wide range of macroeconomic, geopolitical, or sentiment-driven developments could shift the underlying quantity materially in either direction. The asymmetry in the intervals is modest, suggesting I was not strongly weighting tail risks in one particular direction at the time of the forecast.

Beyond the structured uncertainty captured in the intervals, there are tail risks that could push outcomes outside even the 90% bounds. On the downside, an unexpected negative shock — such as a sharp deterioration in economic data, a financial contagion event, or a sudden policy reversal — could drive values well below 520 over the monthly horizon. On the upside, a strong positive catalyst, such as a surprise policy easing, better-than-expected fundamental data, or a relief rally in risk assets, could push the figure above 650. Events with low prior probability but high impact — sometimes called fat-tail risks — are by definition underweighted in confidence intervals constructed around central scenarios, and this forecast is no exception to that limitation.
